patch_description: A fundamentally different approach: instead of Kalman/RTS state-space filtering, use a zero-phase Savitzky-Golay local polynomial smoother (centered, so no phase lag by construction) with an adaptive effective smoothing scale derived from a robust MAD noise estimate, fused via a dynamics-aware blend with a running-median pre-pass. The median pre-pass removes impulsive noise that least-squares polynomials would smear; the Savitzky-Golay pass then fits genuine local dynamics exactly (polynomials reproduce polynomial trends), giving strong noise reduction with minimal lag. A light bidirectional one-pole finish damps residual ripple. Centers near the boundaries use shorter asymmetric polynomial windows so every output sample is supported by real data. This avoids the Kalman lag/overshoot trade-off and the flat-segment artifacts of reversal clamps, directly attacking slope_changes and false_reversals while preserving responsiveness (zero phase) and accuracy.
